title: Keep machine line-ending policy from making committed-input reads falsely dirty
outcome: Resolve the committed-input owner's line-ending normalization contract once so ordinary CRLF checkouts are not silently judged dirty solely because the reader drops the Git configuration used for checkout.
acceptance: A bounded regression establishes the reported system/global core.autocrlf or core.eol checkout/rehash mismatch and distinguishes it from the prior manually rewritten CRLF/stat fixture; a changed-content control still refuses clean credit.

The Engram owner documents and implements one agreed policy for effective line-ending normalization across root and children, with correct local-over-fallback precedence. Prefer matching ordinary effective Git line-ending semantics without admitting unrelated global configuration; if a configuration cannot be represented safely it returns an explicit bounded input_unavailable reason rather than silently conflating normalization mismatch with ordinary not_clean.

The existing shared JSON v1 shape and closed refusal-code set, one shared predicate, strict stderr/deadline/output bounds, no full file/index scan, no inspected-repository/global configuration writes and immutable historical records/evaluations are preserved.

The shared real-Git fixture library and relevant Windows tests exercise the agreed policy; TermAl adapters consume the owner result without adding their own EOL predicate. Required reviews/gates and any acceptance impacts are recorded before delivery.

completion.summary: Fixed false dirty committed-input reads caused by machine Git line-ending policy. Landed, pushed and installed the exact reviewed and fully gated EOL candidate; all six live stores report ready. Actual checkout/rehash, local-over-fallback precedence, recursive mismatch, changed-content and hardening tests passed. Existing JSON, bounds and stored evaluations remain unchanged.
